steps.name: Sample structure QC
steps.question: Do the 3 treated and 3 control liver samples separate by condition in a blind-transformed view, does any sample sit away from its group, and are library sizes comparable?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf

steps.description: Read counts.csv (12000 genes x 6 samples) and metadata.csv (6 rows, condition column); verify sample names match the count columns. Run blind vst in DESeq2, compute a PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap colored by condition, and a library-size table. No test is fitted here.
acceptance_criteria: PCA (top 500 variable genes after blind vst) and sample-distance heatmap produced and colored by condition
Library size table per sample reported with min/median/max depth
Written verdict on whether samples cluster by condition and whether any sample is a candidate outlier, stated before the model runs

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage (treated vs control)
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. The counts arrive as a gene-level Salmon table with no per-sample quantification files and no average-transcript-length table, so fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table and do not invent a length input (R-0169@18ab).

With three replicates per group the test has low power: it finds only a small share of true DE genes, mostly with large fold changes. Keep alpha at 0.05; do not loosen the threshold to compensate. A gene absent from the list is not shown to be unchanged (R-0017@8a47).

DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cooks distance and sets p and padj to NA in cells with fewer than 7 replicates; report these genes apart from independent-filter NAs and inspect the counts of any flagged gene that matters.
steps.context: Raw gene-level Salmon counts as a single gene table; no per-sample quantification files or average-transcript-length table are present, so the length-correction state cannot be established. Design is unpaired 3 vs 3, one batch, no covariates.
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are differentially expressed between drug-treated and control liver samples at adjusted p < 0.05, and with what log2 fold changes?

grounding.reason: Raw counts, unpaired 3 vs 3, no batch or covariates: DESeq2 Wald with apeglm shrinkage per R-0001@9a17; length offset absent per R-0169@18ab

steps.description: Primary differential expression on the count matrix. Pre-filter genes to at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (smallest group size); estimate median-of-ratios size factors; fit ~ condition with condition relevelled so control is the explicit reference; contrast = treated vs control so a positive log2FC means higher in treated. Wald test; keep Cooks-distance outlier flagging (p set to NA in cells with fewer than 7 replicates); report outlier-NA genes separately from independent-filter NA genes. lfcShrink with apeglm for the reported effect; keep the unshrunken log2FC and lfcSE beside it; p-values from the unshrunken fit. Independent filtering on, alpha 0.05 passed to results, BH adjustment, p-value histogram inspected before adjustment.
acceptance_criteria: Full results table with gene, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, and apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange for every tested gene
Counts reported for genes tested after pre-filter, genes with padj < 0.05, genes with NA from outlier flagging, genes with NA from independent filtering
P-value histogram produced and its shape described before the adjusted values are used
Explicit statement in the output that counts were modeled without a length offset (import state unestablished)

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood replication
steps.question: Does an independent count model (edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts and the same treated-vs-control design) call the same genes DE?

grounding.reason: edgeR QL F-test is the prescribed second method at the low replicate end (R-0001@9a17 alternative M-0003); its overlap with DESeq2 defines the high-confidence set (R-0042@54e1)

constraints: Same counts, same design, same alpha as the DESeq2 path
Do not present the union of the two methods as the result; the intersection is the high-confidence set (R-0042@54e1)
steps.description: Second method prescribed for low replicate numbers: TMM normalization, filterByExpr, robust dispersion estimation, quasi-likelihood fit and QL F-test for treated vs control on the same pre-filtered count matrix and design. Output a results table parallel to the DESeq2 table (log2FC unshrunk, FDR) so the two can be compared gene by gene.
acceptance_criteria: Full edgeR results table for the same post-pre-filter gene universe with log2FC, p-value, FDR
Number of edgeR FDR < 0.05 genes reported alongside the DESeq2 count
Per-gene call table (DESeq2 call, edgeR call) written for the intersection computation in T2S2

steps.name: Confidence synthesis: power, method overlap, stability
caveats: The leave-one-out refits are a descriptive stability check on an already-fitted design, not a formal resampling inference procedure; report them as such
Do not change alpha or thresholds in any refit; the power statement is a caution, not a reason to loosen the threshold (R-0017@8a47)
steps.question: How confident can we be in the treated-vs-control gene list given three replicates per group: what effect sizes are detectable, which genes do both methods support, and does the list survive dropping a single sample?

grounding.reason: The power statement and the two-method overlap follow R-0162@ed74, R-0094@6849 and R-0042@54e1; the leave-one-out refit stability check has no covering rule and is planned from knowledge as a descriptive sensitivity analysis, not an inferential one

steps.description: Synthesize the evidence on the n=3 design. (1) Power statement: from the dispersion and depth estimated by the fit, state in closed form the fold change the design can detect with 80 percent power at alpha 0.05 (RNASeqPower and PROPER are not installed; R-0162 prescribes the closed form), and state that adding replicates raises power more than adding depth. (2) Method overlap: intersect DESeq2 padj < 0.05 with edgeR FDR < 0.05; report the intersection as the high-confidence set and the single-method genes as a secondary set labeled by method (R-0042@54e1). (3) Leave-one-out stability: refit the DESeq2 model six times, each dropping one sample, and report for each high-confidence gene the share of refits in which it remains significant at padj < 0.05; summarize the fraction of the high-confidence set retained in at least 5 of 6 refits. (4) Report the lfcSE distribution (approximate 95 percent CI width on log2FC) for the high-confidence genes so the precision of the estimates is visible.
acceptance_criteria: Power statement quantifying the minimum detectable log2 fold change at 80 percent power and alpha 0.05 from the fitted dispersion and observed depth, plus the explicit caution that a gene not found is not shown to be unchanged
High-confidence gene set defined as the DESeq2-edgeR intersection, with counts per method and the overlap; single-method genes listed separately with the method named
Leave-one-out table: per dropped sample, number of significant genes retained; per-gene retention share for high-confidence genes
Summary of lfcSE and CI width for the high-confidence set

steps.name: Report: DE gene list with confidence assessment
steps.question: What is the final treated-vs-control differential expression answer, and what does the report state about the reliability of the n=3 result?
steps.description: Assemble the final report: methods, package versions, design and contrast, thresholds, numbers tested and DE per method; the power statement before the gene tables; MA plot and dispersion plot as fit diagnostics; the gene table carrying unshrunken log2FC, shrunken (apeglm) log2FC, and lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value; the DESeq2-edgeR overlap as the high-confidence set with single-method genes as a secondary list; the leave-one-out stability summary; and a reproducibility record (sessionInfo, seed, package versions).
acceptance_criteria: Report opens with method, package versions, design formula, contrast, thresholds (padj < 0.05), n_tested and n_DE per method, before any gene table
Power statement at n=3 appears before the gene tables, stating that at 3 replicates the count models find a minority of true DE genes, mostly with large fold changes
MA plot and dispersion plot included and described
Gene table carries log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange (estimator named), and lfcSE; genes ranked by the shrunken value; selection strictly by padj
High-confidence (both-method) set, single-method sets, and leave-one-out retention all reported; the union is not presented as the result
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, seed, and package versions stored with the results

plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE with n=3 confidence
plan.analytical_narrative: Raw gene-level Salmon counts for 6 human liver samples (3 drug-treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch, 12000 genes x 6 samples in counts.csv, 6-row condition table in metadata.csv). The question is two-fold: which genes differ between treated and control, and how much confidence n=3 per group supports. The plan follows the grounded two-group count-model procedure: sample-structure QC on blind variance-stabilized values, then a DESeq2 Wald test as the primary model with apeglm fold-change shrinkage, a minimal pre-filter (10 counts in smallest-group-size samples), median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering. Because three replicates per group is the low end of the reliable range and the question explicitly asks about confidence, the plan adds the prescribed second method (edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts and design) and a confidence-synthesis step: a closed-form power statement (RNASeqPower/PROPER are not installed), the DESeq2-edgeR intersection as the high-confidence gene set, and a leave-one-out refit sensitivity check. Caveat carried into the model step: the Salmon counts arrive as a gene-level table with no per-sample quantification files and no average-transcript-length table, so the length correction cannot be established and the model runs on the counts as delivered without a length offset; a change in isoform use can therefore appear as differential expression.

steps.method: blind vst, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library size check
minimal pre-filter: at least 10 counts in as many samples as the smallest group
median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, no pre-normalization
design ~ condition, explicit reference level, gene counts as delivered without length offset, closed-form power statement
DESeq2 Wald test (primary); edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as the second method
Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering; inspect p-value histogram before adjustment
DE report with power statement, two-method overlap as high-confidence set, MA and dispersion diagnostics

plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE with n=3 confidence
plan.analytical_narrative: Raw gene-level Salmon counts for 6 human liver samples (3 drug-treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch, 12000 genes x 6 samples in counts.csv, 6-row condition table in metadata.csv). The question is two-fold: which genes differ between treated and control, and how much confidence n=3 per group supports. The plan follows the grounded two-group count-model procedure: sample-structure QC on blind variance-stabilized values, then a DESeq2 Wald test as the primary model with apeglm fold-change shrinkage, a minimal pre-filter (10 counts in smallest-group-size samples), median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering. Because three replicates per group is the low end of the reliable range and the question explicitly asks about confidence, the plan adds the prescribed second method (edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts and design) and a confidence-synthesis step: a closed-form power statement (RNASeqPower/PROPER are not installed), the DESeq2-edgeR intersection as the high-confidence gene set, and a leave-one-out refit sensitivity check. Caveat carried into the model step: the Salmon counts arrive as a gene-level table with no per-sample quantification files and no average-transcript-length table, so the length correction cannot be established and the model runs on the counts as delivered without a length offset; a change in isoform use can therefore appear as differential expression.

steps.name: Sample structure QC
steps.question: Do the 3 treated and 3 control liver samples separate by condition in a blind-transformed view, does any sample sit away from its group, and are library sizes comparable?
steps.description: Read counts.csv (12000 genes x 6 samples) and metadata.csv (6 rows, condition column); verify sample names match the count columns. Run blind vst in DESeq2, compute a PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap colored by condition, and a library-size table. No test is fitted here.
acceptance_criteria: PCA (top 500 variable genes after blind vst) and sample-distance heatmap produced and colored by condition
Library size table per sample reported with min/median/max depth
Written verdict on whether samples cluster by condition and whether any sample is a candidate outlier, stated before the model runs

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage (treated vs control)
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are differentially expressed between drug-treated and control liver samples at adjusted p < 0.05, and with what log2 fold changes?
steps.description: Primary differential expression on the count matrix. Pre-filter genes to at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (smallest group size); estimate median-of-ratios size factors; fit ~ condition with condition relevelled so control is the explicit reference; contrast = treated vs control so a positive log2FC means higher in treated. Wald test; keep Cooks-distance outlier flagging (p set to NA in cells with fewer than 7 replicates); report outlier-NA genes separately from independent-filter NA genes. lfcShrink with apeglm for the reported effect; keep the unshrunken log2FC and lfcSE beside it; p-values from the unshrunken fit. Independent filtering on, alpha 0.05 passed to results, BH adjustment, p-value histogram inspected before adjustment.
acceptance_criteria: Full results table with gene, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, and apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange for every tested gene
Counts reported for genes tested after pre-filter, genes with padj < 0.05, genes with NA from outlier flagging, genes with NA from independent filtering
P-value histogram produced and its shape described before the adjusted values are used
Explicit statement in the output that counts were modeled without a length offset (import state unestablished)
steps.context: Raw gene-level Salmon counts as a single gene table; no per-sample quantification files or average-transcript-length table are present, so the length-correction state cannot be established. Design is unpaired 3 vs 3, one batch, no covariates.
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. The counts arrive as a gene-level Salmon table with no per-sample quantification files and no average-transcript-length table, so fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table and do not invent a length input (R-0169@18ab).

With three replicates per group the test has low power: it finds only a small share of true DE genes, mostly with large fold changes. Keep alpha at 0.05; do not loosen the threshold to compensate. A gene absent from the list is not shown to be unchanged (R-0017@8a47).

DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cooks distance and sets p and padj to NA in cells with fewer than 7 replicates; report these genes apart from independent-filter NAs and inspect the counts of any flagged gene that matters.

grounding.reason: Raw counts, unpaired 3 vs 3, no batch or covariates: DESeq2 Wald with apeglm shrinkage per R-0001@9a17; length offset absent per R-0169@18ab

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood replication
steps.question: Does an independent count model (edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts and the same treated-vs-control design) call the same genes DE?
steps.description: Second method prescribed for low replicate numbers: TMM normalization, filterByExpr, robust dispersion estimation, quasi-likelihood fit and QL F-test for treated vs control on the same pre-filtered count matrix and design. Output a results table parallel to the DESeq2 table (log2FC unshrunk, FDR) so the two can be compared gene by gene.
acceptance_criteria: Full edgeR results table for the same post-pre-filter gene universe with log2FC, p-value, FDR
Number of edgeR FDR < 0.05 genes reported alongside the DESeq2 count
Per-gene call table (DESeq2 call, edgeR call) written for the intersection computation in T2S2

grounding.reason: edgeR QL F-test is the prescribed second method at the low replicate end (R-0001@9a17 alternative M-0003); its overlap with DESeq2 defines the high-confidence set (R-0042@54e1)

constraints: Same counts, same design, same alpha as the DESeq2 path
Do not present the union of the two methods as the result; the intersection is the high-confidence set (R-0042@54e1)

steps.name: Confidence synthesis: power, method overlap, stability
steps.question: How confident can we be in the treated-vs-control gene list given three replicates per group: what effect sizes are detectable, which genes do both methods support, and does the list survive dropping a single sample?
steps.description: Synthesize the evidence on the n=3 design. (1) Power statement: from the dispersion and depth estimated by the fit, state in closed form the fold change the design can detect with 80 percent power at alpha 0.05 (RNASeqPower and PROPER are not installed; R-0162 prescribes the closed form), and state that adding replicates raises power more than adding depth. (2) Method overlap: intersect DESeq2 padj < 0.05 with edgeR FDR < 0.05; report the intersection as the high-confidence set and the single-method genes as a secondary set labeled by method (R-0042@54e1). (3) Leave-one-out stability: refit the DESeq2 model six times, each dropping one sample, and report for each high-confidence gene the share of refits in which it remains significant at padj < 0.05; summarize the fraction of the high-confidence set retained in at least 5 of 6 refits. (4) Report the lfcSE distribution (approximate 95 percent CI width on log2FC) for the high-confidence genes so the precision of the estimates is visible.
acceptance_criteria: Power statement quantifying the minimum detectable log2 fold change at 80 percent power and alpha 0.05 from the fitted dispersion and observed depth, plus the explicit caution that a gene not found is not shown to be unchanged
High-confidence gene set defined as the DESeq2-edgeR intersection, with counts per method and the overlap; single-method genes listed separately with the method named
Leave-one-out table: per dropped sample, number of significant genes retained; per-gene retention share for high-confidence genes
Summary of lfcSE and CI width for the high-confidence set
caveats: The leave-one-out refits are a descriptive stability check on an already-fitted design, not a formal resampling inference procedure; report them as such
Do not change alpha or thresholds in any refit; the power statement is a caution, not a reason to loosen the threshold (R-0017@8a47)

grounding.reason: The power statement and the two-method overlap follow R-0162@ed74, R-0094@6849 and R-0042@54e1; the leave-one-out refit stability check has no covering rule and is planned from knowledge as a descriptive sensitivity analysis, not an inferential one

steps.name: Report: DE gene list with confidence assessment
steps.question: What is the final treated-vs-control differential expression answer, and what does the report state about the reliability of the n=3 result?
steps.description: Assemble the final report: methods, package versions, design and contrast, thresholds, numbers tested and DE per method; the power statement before the gene tables; MA plot and dispersion plot as fit diagnostics; the gene table carrying unshrunken log2FC, shrunken (apeglm) log2FC, and lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value; the DESeq2-edgeR overlap as the high-confidence set with single-method genes as a secondary list; the leave-one-out stability summary; and a reproducibility record (sessionInfo, seed, package versions).
acceptance_criteria: Report opens with method, package versions, design formula, contrast, thresholds (padj < 0.05), n_tested and n_DE per method, before any gene table
Power statement at n=3 appears before the gene tables, stating that at 3 replicates the count models find a minority of true DE genes, mostly with large fold changes
MA plot and dispersion plot included and described
Gene table carries log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange (estimator named), and lfcSE; genes ranked by the shrunken value; selection strictly by padj
High-confidence (both-method) set, single-method sets, and leave-one-out retention all reported; the union is not presented as the result
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, seed, and package versions stored with the results

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.

steps.method: blind vst, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library size check
minimal pre-filter: at least 10 counts in as many samples as the smallest group
median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, no pre-normalization
design ~ condition, explicit reference level, gene counts as delivered without length offset, closed-form power statement
DESeq2 Wald test (primary); edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as the second method
Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering; inspect p-value histogram before adjustment
DE report with power statement, two-method overlap as high-confidence set, MA and dispersion diagnostics
